visual_thesis: A plain-language executive summary before final verification gives the owner a useful point to approve, redirect or stop long agent work.
mechanism_metaphor: An oversized single executive-summary proof sheet lies diagonally across an interrupted work ribbon, not a generic card dashboard. On the sheet exactly five large named fields make the review content visible: goal, changes, tradeoffs, risks and proposed checks. Each field contains its exact word label only, no invented example record or micro-writing. The incoming work ribbon stops at this sheet. Three clearly differentiated decision branches on the right lead to final verification, return for revision, or a blunt stopped end. The labels Approve, Redirect and Stop explain their meaning; approval alone reaches the verification page. A red-pencil bracket visibly marks the pause, without a hand, signature or completed-check success badge. White paper and refined graphite illustration; text architecture is integrated proof editing, not plaques.
